items.briefing:
Australians are being warned about a surge in celebrity impersonation scams, with YouTube star MrBeast currently the most commonly used identity by scammers, according to Malwarebytes. These scams typically promise fake giveaways or prizes to trick people into handing over money or personal details. Staff should be cautious of any unsolicited messages or social media posts featuring celebrities offering rewards, even if they look convincing.

Security researchers are also highlighting growing threats linked to AI, particularly around stolen or misused digital identities. Being alert to unusual account activity and using strong, unique passwords remains more important than ever.

**Practical tip:** If you see a celebrity giveaway online, assume it's a scam — legitimate competitions are never run through direct messages or unofficial pages.

featured.title: MrBeast tops impersonation scams, Malwarebytes says
featured.summary: Fraudsters are timing texts for lunch and Fridays, as MrBeast led impersonation scams in Malwarebytes' three-month global study.
